sources.name: Talker Research: America's all-time favorite movies, n=2,000 US adults, Jan 31-Feb 3 2025
sources.method: Top 20 as published (ties at 12% taken in listed order). Series entries mapped to flagship film (Star Wars, Indiana Jones to Raiders, Jurassic Park). Missing = 25.

sources.name: YouGov Ratings: most popular all-time movies in America
sources.method: Share with a positive opinion; top 20 only (page data confirmed in the HTML). Skews family/holiday films. Missing = 25.

sources.name: Wikipedia: highest-grossing films in US and Canada, adjusted for ticket-price inflation (top 30; a 2026 release that is still in theaters was ignored)
sources.method: Domestic box office attendance proxy, ranks 1-30. Missing = 35. Only counts films a lot of people paid to see; favors 1930s-70s epics.

sources.name: IMDb Top 250 (user ratings), read via r.jina.ai mirror
sources.method: Ranks 1-250 read live today; ranks capped at 35, absent = 35. Rating-weighted, so it favors acclaimed films over broad favorites.

changes_vs_current: Critic canon replaced by people picks: Forrest Gump, Titanic, Lion King, Wizard of Oz, Gone with the Wind, Sound of Music, Home Alone, Toy Story, Ten Commandments, Dirty Dancing, Ghostbusters enter; Shawshank and Dark Knight stay (8th, 16th); Seven Samurai, City Lights, Psycho, Apocalypse Now, Vertigo, Citizen Kane, Casablanca, Pulp Fiction, Goodfellas, Fight Club, Matrix, Inception, Gladiator, Saving Private Ryan and Fight Club drop out.
confidence: medium. Top 10 passes the 'typical adult at a party' check: Gump, Godfather, Star Wars, Titanic, Lion King, Wizard of Oz, Gone with the Wind, Shawshank, Jurassic Park, Sound of Music. Weak spots: (1) positions 12-24 are near-tied (19.0 to 21.6) and mostly rest on 1-2 sources, so order there is soft; (2) The Ten Commandments (#20) is a box-office-only artifact of the inflation-adjusted list (Doctor Zhivago, Exorcist, Snow White sat just behind it) and a hand swap to Pulp Fiction, Fight Club, Matrix, or Inception would likely suit casual players better; (3) the Harris poll is 12 years old and was read second-hand; (4) the 2014-2025 polls are only top 10-20, so the missing-penalty rule does a lot of the work. Ties broken by source count, then critic standing from the prior research file (not re-fetched): Godfather before Star Wars, Return of the King before Home Alone, Jaws before Dirty Dancing. No Morning Consult or Harris 2020s all-time poll exists to corroborate.
